title: One key shape for per-IP limits
evidence: The app routes key their per-IP limits on the /64 bucket (ipBucket in app-gate.server.ts; app-routes.server.ts, api.chat.ts web turns), while other per-IP limiters key on the address as read (api.feedback, api.events, api.ab, api.measurements, api.google-token, api.lab-import-v2). Use one key shape for all. From the PR 1613 review. Design note docs/drafts/s-21-ip-key-design.md (owner rulings 2026-11-14). PR 1a of the series (1665): address keys normalised before use, the shape of the forwarded header counted (numbers only), an over-limit quota charge refused before it touches the map (US-52 AC4g-AC4i). PR 1b (1667): the forwarded hop read only where Fly writes its entry (AC4j), merging after the count is read. Verify at batch end: a normal storefront chat and lab upload are not refused; the 429 rate on those routes does not jump; the hourly forwarded-shape line appears in the logs. PR 2 (2026-11-25, US-52 AC4k): every per-IP limit builds its key with the one helper, clientKey(request, trust) in app/lib/ip-key.server.ts (ipBucket moved there from app-gate.server.ts): feedback, events, ab, email capture, lab upload files, google token, reminders requests and opt-in (hashed bucket), guest sessions (hashed bucket; the session stays bound to the address, owner ruling 2a), mcp authorize, mcp rate-limit events, mcp reviewer failures. mcp token stays on the address (owner ruling 1b), through allowTokenFrom in mcp-grants.server.ts. No count or window changed; which header is trusted did not change. Left: PR 1b (1667, AC4j) and S-21b
durability_check: Per-IP limiters are declared on the branded IpKey type, which only ip-key.server.ts makes (a raw string is a type error); app/lib/ip-key.guard.test.ts fails on a getClientIp call outside the named list, an IpKey cast outside the helper, or a per-IP limiter not declared on IpKey
